findings.source_quote: ὑπέρ τε τοῦ κοινοῦ ἢ συμφέροντος τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν τάξιν προσομιλήσας
findings.english_quote: He discussed the order that served the common or beneficial interest of the assembly and advised them to obey Maron the overseer.
findings.issue: “That served” makes the common or beneficial interest a property of the order, rather than the concern or purpose of Peter’s address. The draft also treats τὴν τάξιν exclusively as the arrangement discussed, without disclosing the material alternative that it denotes the constituted body or order being addressed. The existing note preserves ἢ but does not explain these attachment and lexical choices. This is a translation issue, not evidence of corrupt or unverified print.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove “that served” and attach the interest phrase to Peter’s speaking. A proposed rendering is: “He addressed the constituted body concerning the common or beneficial interest of the assembly and advised them to obey Maron the overseer.” Add a source-quoted note explaining the body/order interpretation of τάξις in the context of the preceding institutional appointments, while preserving the alternative interpretation of speech about organizational arrangements. Also distinguish topical “concerning” from purposive “for the benefit of” for ὑπέρ. The proposed replacement requires fresh review.
